Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-04] Learner-facing language follows the course setting. For the first course (UPSC / State PCS) it is Hinglish: natural Hindi sentence flow, English technical terms, the way Navin teaches.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.
[G-07] Two layers, like a film (Navin, 24 October 2026). The writer layer (understanding, plan, script) decides what is said and how deep, following the level profile and the book's own level. The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.
[S2-01] Plan the chapter's videos from the chapter map: first one short 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video (5-8 minutes) that teaches the chapter's prerequisites, then the topic videos in teaching order. Narration is 6-8 minutes per book page (Navin, 23 October 2026; the 14-page tissue chapter about 85-110 minutes of topic videos, plus the prerequisite video): each topic video gets the share of the pages its items come from, and a very dense page may go up to 25% over when the plan says why. Understanding (Section 1) and the chapter map have no time limit.
[S2-02] Write a spoken teacher script in beats with a natural teacher flow. Stories and analogies only where they genuinely help that topic. Every item the book teaches is taught and every teacher question answered from the book is answered; questions answered from outside the book are used only where they help and the time allows. Cut repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[S2-03] Prerequisites are only what this chapter directly needs, never a prerequisite of a prerequisite. They are taught, not named, in the chapter's 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video, each with a simple explanation and an example; a topic video may remind of them in at most 2 beats.
[S2-04] Spoken Hinglish the way Navin teaches, in mixed script (Navin, 21 and 23 October 2026): Hindi words in Devanagari, English words, above all the book's technical terms, in Roman exactly as the book spells them, as in 'आज हम tissue के बारे में पढ़ेंगे'; a genuinely difficult Hindi word (formal, literary or technical; not in BIE's everyday word list rulebook/simple_hindi.json) gets its English word in brackets right after it, as in 'सतह (surface)'; the screen and subtitles show the bracket and the voice says 'सतह, यानी surface'. Never a bracket after an everyday word or inside an idiom or a fixed phrase ('आम तौर पर', not 'आम तौर (usually) पर'; 'नहीं के बराबर', not 'नहीं के बराबर (equal to)'). Never an English term in Devanagari or a Hindi word in Roman. Numbers as digits; short spoken sentences addressed to one student; questions to the student and natural pauses; no reading out of lists.
[S2-05] Every beat states which chapter-map items it covers and which teacher questions it answers, and those claims must be true: the beat really explains that item and really answers that question.
[S2-06] Teach every part of a video through the universal frame (what the process is, how it works, when and in what order, under which conditions, in what atmosphere) and through the teaching pattern of its content type, step by step in the pattern's order; every item on the task card is really taught, none only named.
[S2-07] Open every book line in the script, never read it out (Navin, 24 October 2026). A new topic opens with a question about something the learner can see, then the name. After any book line the beat carries at least one of: the term's plain meaning with 'yaani' and an everyday image, a why step from a need, an example or the place. Speak complete sentences, not clipped notes. A classification is taught as a family: the overview tree, then every member in the same slots (layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence), then the members compared and a memory trick. BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the result first (what it makes). 2) inputs and the place. 3) each step with its cause and its condition. 4) what breaks when a step fails. 5) the whole run once more at speed. 6) recap as a flow.
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the whole in context. 2) zoom into each part in a fixed path (outside to inside). 3) function of each part tied to its shape. 4) how the parts work together. 5) labelled recap.
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the overview tree first: the basis of division and every member named. 2) every member in the same slots: layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence. 3) the members compared side by side, the most confused pair named directly. 4) a memory trick for the family.
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what is common. 2) criteria one at a time, both sides together. 3) the reason behind each difference. 4) the most confused pair named directly. 5) difference table as recap.
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the period and its atmosphere. 2) events in order with their causes. 3) the people and their choices. 4) the turning point. 5) what changed after. 6) timeline recap.
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the effect students can see. 2) the cause. 3) each link of the chain with its mechanism. 4) the evidence. 5) the exception or limit. 6) the chain as recap.
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the fact in one line. 2) the number shown to scale against something familiar. 3) where it comes from (book or outside, dated). 4) what it changes or proves. 5) a formula built term by term when there is one.
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what the figure is and why it is here. 2) a reading path across it (labels in order). 3) the one thing to remember from it. 4) link back to the text it explains.
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) a concrete example first. 2) the book's definition word by word. 3) a non-example that tests the boundary. 4) where the term is used next in the chapter.

How real teachers open a book line (teacher example bank 2026-10-29.1; use these ways, in your own words):
- Open with a question on something visible (every new topic and every new family member): Skin aur stomach, kidney ke upar ek outer layer hai ki nahi? Yeh kis se bani hai? — phir naam: epithelial tissue.
- One everyday image per shape or function (every term that names a shape, a layer or a job): Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
- The word root where it helps (a term whose parts carry its meaning): Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
- Why starts from a need (every why step): Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
- Contrast with the neighbour (members of one family, and what the exam confuses): Simple epithelium ka kaam protection nahi, woh compound ka hai. Zyada layers = pathogen andar nahi aata.
- Ask and repeat the key word (the one word the learner must keep): Irregular walls. Kaisi? Irregular.
- Exam memory beats by level (after the understanding, by the level profile): Yaad rakhna: brush border PCT mein. Doosre naam: pavement, tessellated. M2B = muscle to bone = tendon, B2B = bone to bone = ligament.
- Link to something already known (a new place or a new structure): Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
- Meaning with two or three real examples (an abstract word in the book): Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
- Open the book's adjective (Navin's example) (a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is): Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. Video v5: Gold link टूटा, फिर भी dollar की माँग क्यों रही?
Goal: Learner Bretton Woods का US$35 gold link, Triffin contradiction, 1971 decision और petrodollars से continuing dollar demand की causal chains समझेगा।
Opening hook: दुनिया को trade के लिए और dollars चाहिए, लेकिन हर dollar के gold में बदलने का भरोसा भी चाहिए—तनाव कहाँ बनेगा?
Story or analogy: Dollar availability और gold-conversion confidence को 2 अलग जरूरतों की तरह दिखाएँगे। हर causal link के बाद उसका नतीजा जोड़ेंगे; gold link समाप्त होने और dollar demand समाप्त होने को अलग रखेंगे।
Planned minutes: 6
Narration time (S2-01): 5.3-7.1 minutes, about 689-923 spoken words (BIE counts 130 words a minute)
Prerequisites already taught in the prerequisite video (remind of one in at most 2 beats): Purchases, prices, debts and payments due later; Bank balances, deposits, loans and interest; Denominations, monetary arithmetic, percentages and minimum–maximum limits; Purchasing power, inflation, scarcity and liquidity; Central bank, commercial bank, government treasury and bank-to-bank settlement; Foreign currencies, exchange rates, reserves and demand–supply changes; Chronological reading: BCE/CE, centuries, dynasties and law versus implementation dates; Digital instructions, identity authentication, ledgers and payment interfaces
Open every book line (S2-07): a question about something the learner can see, then the name; every term opened: its plain meaning with 'yaani' and one everyday image (the word root where it helps); the why, starting from a need or a problem, one link at a time; an example or the place, by a zoom from the organ or the thing the learner knows; the consequence: what follows, and the link to the previous or the next idea; the contrast: what it is not, and what the exam confuses it with; the memory beat by level: the exam's 'yaad rakhna', the other names, the trick.

p005-i12 | 5 | heading | timeline | The Bretton Woods System (1944) and its End (1971)
  p005-i12#q1 | when | Which years frame the system in the heading? → The heading identifies the system with 1944 and its end with 1971. | book
  p005-i12#q2 | why | Why does the page move from the arrangement to its end? → It first describes gold conversion and the Dollar's reserve role, then explains excess Dollars, pressure for gold and Nixon's termination of convertibility. | book
  p005-i12#q3 | how | How should the heading's 'end' be read precisely? → The specific 1971 event described here is the end of Dollar–gold convertibility. Do not treat the heading as a statement that every related institution disappeared then. | outside
  term | Bretton Woods System | yaani देशों के पैसे जोड़ने का ऐसा ढाँचा जिसमें Dollar का gold से संबंध था | image: gold से Dollar और Dollar से बाकी currencies की जुड़ी कड़ियाँ
  why | International payments need a monetary arrangement that participants trust. [standard] → This page follows the gold–Dollar arrangement into the pressures that ended convertibility. [book]
  example or place | Timeline from 1944 through the 1960s to 15 August 1971.
  consequence | The learner can locate the monetary mechanism and its breakdown in time.
  visual | Extend a timeline from 1944 to 1971.
  level extra | Distinguish the historical system from the continuing existence of institutions associated with Bretton Woods.
p005-i13 | 5 | list_point | facts_numbers | US promised to convert US$35 into one troy ounce of gold. This promise applied mainly to foreign central banks
  p005-i13#q1 | what | What promise anchored the Dollar? → The US promised one troy ounce of gold for US$35, with the promise applying mainly to foreign central banks. | book
  p005-i13#q2 | evidence | What prevents interpreting this as a universal retail gold-exchange facility? → The page qualifies the promise with 'mainly to foreign central banks', identifying official foreign holders as its principal beneficiaries. | book
  p005-i13#q3 | why | Why could this promise support confidence? → An eligible official holder could exchange a specified Dollar claim for a specified mass of gold. Confidence depended on the authority's capacity and willingness to honour that promise. | outside
  p005-i13#q4 | how | How much gold would US$350 obtain at the printed rate? → In an illustrative eligible official conversion, US$350 divided by US$35 per troy ounce gives 10 troy ounces. Dollar claims fall as gold is transferred to the holder. | outside
  p005-i13#q5 | what | What is a troy ounce? → It is a precious-metal mass unit of approximately 31.1 grams, not a currency unit. | outside
  term | convert | yaani तय नियम से Dollars देकर gold लेना | image: एक तरफ Dollar वाला दावा घटे, दूसरी तरफ gold आए
  term | troy ounce | yaani gold जैसी धातु तौलने की वजन वाली unit | image: जौहरी की तराजू पर रखा gold
  term | foreign central banks | yaani US के बाहर दूसरे देशों के central banks | image: व्यक्ति की बजाय देशों की monetary authorities के बीच लेन-देन
  why | Foreign official holders need confidence in the Dollars they retain. [standard] → The specified gold exchange supplies a concrete anchor for those claims. [standard]
  example or place | Hypothetical official French conversion under the historical arrangement; quantities below are illustrative.
  consequence | Conversion transfers gold out of US reserves and reduces the converting authority's Dollar claims.
  visual | Exchange US$350 of official claims for 10 troy ounces.
  level extra | This is a historical official mechanism, not a present-day Indian bank service or a retail entitlement.
  real world (run it first, with these numbers, then name the term) | place: Historical US–France official monetary settlement, with hypothetical quantities | actors: French monetary authority, US monetary authority | goods: official Dollar claims, gold | numbers: French Dollar claims used in conversion US$350 → US$0; gold received in this transaction 0 troy ounces → 10 troy ounces
    step 1 | An eligible French monetary authority presents US$350 of claims for official conversion. | shows: An eligible holder invokes the promised fixed conversion rate.
    step 2 | The US authority transfers 10 troy ounces and extinguishes the US$350 claim used. | shows: US$35 per troy ounce determines the gold transfer and draws down US gold.
    then the name | This exchange illustrates fixed gold convertibility.
    real life | The transaction makes the page's account of France demanding gold understandable; these quantities are not historical evidence.
p005-i14 | 5 | list_point | facts_numbers | The Dollar became the world's reserve currency.
  p005-i14#q1 | what | What international role did the Dollar acquire? → It became the world's reserve currency in the arrangement described. | book
  p005-i14#q2 | evidence | What other material on the page supports its central role? → The diagram places the Dollar between gold and other currencies, while the Triffin bullets identify the world's need for Dollars for international trade. | book
  p005-i14#q3 | how | How does reserve-currency use enter an import payment? → A monetary authority can supply foreign-currency balances through the banking system for an external payment. If it supplies Dollars from reserves without offsetting inflows, its Dollar reserve balance falls as the foreign seller receives payment. | outside
  p005-i14#q4 | why | Why does expanding trade matter for reserve demand? → Larger external obligations can require larger internationally usable payment balances. This helps explain why the world sought more Dollars, although the currency used for any particular transaction depends on its arrangements. | outside
  term | reserve currency | yaani जिस currency में monetary authorities international payments के लिए इस्तेमाल हो सकने वाले assets रखती हैं | image: विदेश का bill चुकाने के लिए रखा Dollar balance
  why | Import bills and other external obligations require internationally usable balances. [standard] → Holding reserve-currency assets helps meet those obligations and creates demand for that currency. [standard]
  example or place | Hypothetical French payment for US machinery using official Dollar reserves through banks.
  consequence | The Dollar's international usefulness creates demand for its supply, linking to Triffin's contradiction.
  visual | Move Dollars from a reserve account through banks to an exporter.
  level extra | A reserve is a stock of assets; an import payment is a flow that may reduce that stock.
  real world (run it first, with these numbers, then name the term) | place: Historical France–US machinery trade, with hypothetical quantities | actors: French importer, French commercial bank, French monetary authority, US machinery exporter | goods: machinery, Dollar reserve balances, import payment | numbers: French official Dollar reserves without offsetting inflows US$700 → US$350; exporter's receipts from this payment US$0 → US$350
    step 1 | A French importer pays the domestic-currency equivalent through its bank for a US$350 machinery invoice; the monetary authority supplies Dollars from reserves. | shows: Official foreign-currency assets provide internationally usable settlement balances.
    step 2 | The bank transfers US$350 to the US exporter; without offsetting inflows, official Dollar reserves fall from US$700 to US$350. | shows: Using reserve balances settles external obligations and reduces the available reserve stock.
    then the name | The Dollar's role in such official holdings and international settlement illustrates a reserve currency.
    real life | This hypothetical transaction opens the page's link between Dollar reserves and international trade; it is not a reported historical trade.
p005-i15 | 5 | list_point | cause_effect | By the 1960s: US spent heavily on Vietnam War and welfare programs. More Dollars circulated worldwide than the gold available in US reserves. France began demanding gold instead of Dollars.
  p005-i15#q1 | why | Why did the gold-conversion commitment come under pressure? → The page lists heavy US spending on the Vietnam War and welfare programs, worldwide Dollars exceeding available US reserve gold, and France demanding gold instead of Dollars. | book
  p005-i15#q2 | how | How do growing external Dollar claims strain unchanged gold reserves? → At a fixed conversion rate, more eligible Dollar claims mean more gold would be needed if holders sought conversion. When available gold does not rise sufficiently, confidence in full redemption can weaken and encourage demands for gold. | outside
  p005-i15#q3 | how | How should Dollars and gold be compared? → Convert Dollar claims into the gold required at US$35 per troy ounce, then compare that requirement with available gold. A raw Dollar count cannot be compared directly with a mass of gold. | outside
  p005-i15#q4 | why | Does every Dollar of domestic US spending automatically become a foreign claim? → No. International payments and external imbalances are the connecting channels. Domestic spending alone does not identify how many Dollars accumulate abroad. | outside
  p005-i15#q5 | when | When does the page locate these pressures? → By the 1960s, before Nixon's 1971 decision. | book
  term | US reserves | yaani US के पास रखा gold का भंडार, जिससे conversion का वादा निभाया जाता | image: बढ़ते दावों के पीछे रखा सीमित gold stock
  why | Foreign official holders need confidence that their Dollar claims can be redeemed as promised. [standard] → Growing claims against limited gold make conversion demands a threat to the available backing. [standard]
  example or place | Hypothetical US payments for French machinery and subsequent official gold demand, situated in the historical arrangement.
  consequence | Gold demands can reduce the very reserves supporting confidence and expose the arrangement's vulnerability.
  visual | Increase foreign Dollar balances against unchanged gold, then draw gold out.
  level extra | All example quantities are illustrative; external payment flows, not domestic spending alone, create the foreign balance in the story.
  real world (run it first, with these numbers, then name the term) | place: Historical US–France machinery trade and official settlement, with hypothetical quantities | actors: US importer, French machinery exporter, French banks, French monetary authority, US monetary authority | goods: machinery, Dollar claims, gold | numbers: French official Dollar claims after acquisition of export proceeds US$350 → US$700; US gold before any conversion in this illustration 10 troy ounces → 10 troy ounces; gold needed to redeem those claims fully 10 troy ounces → 20 troy ounces
    step 1 | A US importer pays US$350 for French machinery. The exporter exchanges the proceeds through French banks, and the French monetary authority acquires the Dollars, raising its illustrative holdings from US$350 to US$700. | shows: Cross-border payments can add to foreign official Dollar claims.
    step 2 | US gold stays at 10 troy ounces, while redeeming US$700 at the printed rate would require 20 ounces. | shows: Claims grow without matching gold, straining the conversion promise.
    step 3 | If the French authority converts US$350, it receives 10 ounces, leaving the illustrative US stock exhausted while US$350 of its claims remains. | shows: Actual redemption draws down scarce backing and exposes vulnerability.
    then the name | This transaction illustrates pressure on gold convertibility from growing external Dollar claims.
    real life | It explains the mechanism behind the page's statement that France demanded gold; it does not report actual French balances or US gold stocks.
p005-i16 | 5 | diagram | figure | Three vertically connected boxes: Gold (US$35 per ounce) at the top; a downward arrow leads to US Dollar in the middle; another downward arrow leads to Other currencies (Pound, Rupee, Yen, Franc, etc.) at the bottom. The diagram shows gold anchoring the Dollar and other currencies linked through the Dollar.
  p005-i16#q1 | what | What relationship does the diagram show? → Gold is the top anchor, the US Dollar is the intermediate currency, and other currencies occupy the bottom level connected through the Dollar. | book
  p005-i16#q2 | which | Which other currencies are explicitly named? → Pound, Rupee, Yen and Franc, followed by 'etc.' to indicate further currencies. | book
  p005-i16#q3 | how | How should the downward arrows be read? → They show the monetary anchoring hierarchy, not physical shipments of gold through every country. In the standard Bretton Woods explanation, currencies maintained fixed but adjustable parities in a Dollar-centred arrangement. | outside
  term | Other currencies | yaani Dollar के अलावा देशों में चलने वाले पैसे, जैसे Rupee और Yen | image: अलग-अलग देशों के notes एक Dollar वाले जोड़ से जुड़े
  why | Different national currencies need an international value relationship. [standard] → The diagram organizes that relationship as gold → Dollar → other currencies. [book]
  example or place | The diagram explicitly includes the Rupee among other currencies.
  consequence | Breaking the gold–Dollar link affects the anchor underlying the arrangement.
  visual | Trace the two arrows from gold through the Dollar to the other currencies.
  level extra | Arrows show linkage, not a historical sequence in which currencies were created.
p005-i17 | 5 | diagram_label | figure | Gold (US$35 per ounce): names the top anchor box; its downward arrow points to US Dollar.
  p005-i17#q1 | what | What is the top box's role? → It identifies gold as the anchor and states US$35 per ounce. | book
  p005-i17#q2 | which | Which text clarifies the type of ounce used here? → The nearby bullet specifies one troy ounce, supplying the fuller unit for the diagram's abbreviated 'ounce'. | book
  p005-i17#q3 | how | How does the price connect gold to the next box? → The conversion promise fixes the amount of gold associated with an eligible Dollar claim, providing the Dollar with its gold anchor. | outside
  term | US$35 per ounce | yaani एक ounce gold के बदले US$35; पास के text में troy ounce लिखा है | image: gold के एक तय वजन पर Dollar का tag
  why | A fixed conversion promise needs a stated quantity and price. [standard] → The top label supplies that numerical gold anchor. [book]
  example or place | Top box of the Bretton Woods diagram.
  consequence | Sets the benchmark against which convertibility pressure is understood.
  visual | Attach the US$35 tag to one troy ounce of gold.
  level extra | Do not silently drop the troy qualification from the associated text.
p005-i18 | 5 | diagram_label | figure | US Dollar: names the middle box, receiving a downward arrow from Gold and sending a downward arrow to Other currencies.
  p005-i18#q1 | what | What does the middle box represent? → It represents the US Dollar as the connecting currency between the gold anchor and the other currencies. | book
  p005-i18#q2 | which | Which two levels connect through it? → Gold above and Other currencies below. | book
  p005-i18#q3 | why | Why is its central position important? → It makes the Dollar's credibility relevant beyond the US: currencies linked through it depend on the stability of the central monetary anchor. | outside

  p005-i19#q1 | what | What does the lowest box collect together? → Currencies other than the US Dollar, with Pound, Rupee, Yen and Franc named as examples. | book
  p005-i19#q2 | which | Which box is their immediate connection in the diagram? → The US Dollar box, not a separate direct arrow from the gold box. | book

  example or place | Rupee is the familiar Indian example explicitly printed in the box.
  consequence | Domestic currency use should not be confused with direct individual access to US gold.
  visual | Fan out the Pound, Rupee, Yen and Franc cards beneath the Dollar.

p005-i20 | 5 | list_point | cause_effect | Economist Robert Triffin predicted a built-in contradiction. The world needed more Dollars for international trade. Supplying more Dollars weakened confidence in their gold convertibility.
  p005-i20#q1 | why | Why was there a built-in contradiction? → World trade needed more Dollars, but supplying more Dollars weakened confidence in their gold convertibility. | book
  p005-i20#q2 | how | How do international liquidity and confidence conflict? → Providing more Dollar balances supports international payments but increases external claims potentially convertible into gold. If gold does not grow sufficiently, confidence weakens. Restraining external Dollar supply can protect the conversion commitment while failing to meet growing liquidity needs. | outside
  p005-i20#q3 | who | Who predicted the contradiction? → Economist Robert Triffin. | book
  p005-i20#q4 | consequence | Why is this more than a problem caused by one gold demand? → The tension arises from the reserve issuer's dual task: supplying international liquidity while maintaining confidence in promised backing. frame.process: Trace the gold–Dollar arrangement from 1944 to the termination of convertibility in 1971.
frame.how: Explain the original anchor, accumulating pressures and Nixon's decision.
frame.when: 1944, the 1960s and 15 August 1971, in that order.
frame.conditions: Confidence depends on the credibility of the official gold-conversion promise.
frame.atmosphere: International trade needs usable balances while official holders seek dependable backing.

frame.process: Explain the conversion rate and the Dollar's reserve-currency role.
frame.how: Build conversion arithmetic and distinguish reserve assets from payments using them.
frame.when: Under the historical gold-linked arrangement, before the 1971 break.
frame.conditions: Conversion applied mainly to foreign central banks; numerical transactions are hypothetical.
frame.atmosphere: French and US authorities settle gold claims and machinery payments through banks.

frame.process: Explain why increasing external Dollar claims strained confidence in gold redemption.
frame.how: Compare the gold needed for claims with available gold, then contrast liquidity with confidence.
frame.when: Pressures accumulated by the 1960s, before the 1971 decision.
frame.conditions: The conflict appears when external claims grow without sufficient growth in gold.
frame.atmosphere: Trade expands while official holders worry about the conversion promise.

frame.process: Read the gold–Dollar–other currencies hierarchy.
frame.how: Trace the three boxes and two arrows from top to bottom.
frame.when: Read as a relationship within the arrangement, not a chronology.
frame.conditions: Arrows indicate monetary links, not physical gold shipments or retail conversion rights.
frame.atmosphere: A three-level diagram connects a familiar Rupee to the international monetary anchor.

frame.process: Connect the 1973 oil shock with the 1974 Saudi–US understanding.
frame.how: Explain restricted supply, higher prices, Saudi financial commitments and US security commitments.
frame.when: 1973 precedes the 1974 understanding.
frame.conditions: Pricing and investment are separate commitments; illustrative allocations are not historical shares.
frame.atmosphere: Oil importers face expensive supplies while Saudi Arabia and the US exchange financial and security commitments.

frame.process: Explain continuing Dollar demand from oil-payment requirements.
frame.how: Follow an enlarged Dollar invoice through a bank into payment demand.
frame.when: After gold convertibility ends, whenever oil invoices require Dollars.
frame.conditions: Dollar pricing is neither oil redemption nor a guarantee of exchange-value stability.
frame.atmosphere: An Indian oil importer obtains foreign currency to pay a seller.

frame.process: Answer why Dollars could still be held without gold backing.
frame.how: Apply the distinction between redemption backing and transaction demand.
frame.when: After teaching the oil-payment channel.
frame.conditions: The invoice specifies Dollars even though gold conversion is unavailable.
frame.atmosphere: A conceptual exam question tests whether the learner confuses backing with usefulness.

frame.process: Trace the gold–Dollar arrangement from 1944 to the termination of convertibility in 1971.
frame.how: Explain the original anchor, accumulating pressures and Nixon's decision.
frame.when: 1944, the 1960s and 15 August 1971, in that order.
frame.conditions: Confidence depends on the credibility of the official gold-conversion promise.
frame.atmosphere: International trade needs usable balances while official holders seek dependable backing.

frame.process: Explain the conversion rate and the Dollar's reserve-currency role.
frame.how: Build conversion arithmetic and distinguish reserve assets from payments using them.
frame.when: Under the historical gold-linked arrangement, before the 1971 break.
frame.conditions: Conversion applied mainly to foreign central banks; numerical transactions are hypothetical.
frame.atmosphere: French and US authorities settle gold claims and machinery payments through banks.

frame.process: Explain why increasing external Dollar claims strained confidence in gold redemption.
frame.how: Compare the gold needed for claims with available gold, then contrast liquidity with confidence.
frame.when: Pressures accumulated by the 1960s, before the 1971 decision.
frame.conditions: The conflict appears when external claims grow without sufficient growth in gold.
frame.atmosphere: Trade expands while official holders worry about the conversion promise.

frame.process: Read the gold–Dollar–other currencies hierarchy.
frame.how: Trace the three boxes and two arrows from top to bottom.
frame.when: Read as a relationship within the arrangement, not a chronology.
frame.conditions: Arrows indicate monetary links, not physical gold shipments or retail conversion rights.
frame.atmosphere: A three-level diagram connects a familiar Rupee to the international monetary anchor.

frame.process: Connect the 1973 oil shock with the 1974 Saudi–US understanding.
frame.how: Explain restricted supply, higher prices, Saudi financial commitments and US security commitments.
frame.when: 1973 precedes the 1974 understanding.
frame.conditions: Pricing and investment are separate commitments; illustrative allocations are not historical shares.
frame.atmosphere: Oil importers face expensive supplies while Saudi Arabia and the US exchange financial and security commitments.

frame.process: Explain continuing Dollar demand from oil-payment requirements.
frame.how: Follow an enlarged Dollar invoice through a bank into payment demand.
frame.when: After gold convertibility ends, whenever oil invoices require Dollars.
frame.conditions: Dollar pricing is neither oil redemption nor a guarantee of exchange-value stability.
frame.atmosphere: An Indian oil importer obtains foreign currency to pay a seller.

frame.process: Answer why Dollars could still be held without gold backing.
frame.how: Apply the distinction between redemption backing and transaction demand.
frame.when: After teaching the oil-payment channel.
frame.conditions: The invoice specifies Dollars even though gold conversion is unavailable.
frame.atmosphere: A conceptual exam question tests whether the learner confuses backing with usefulness.

frame.process: Trace the gold–Dollar arrangement from 1944 to the termination of convertibility in 1971.
frame.how: Explain the original anchor, accumulating pressures and Nixon's decision.
frame.when: 1944, the 1960s and 15 August 1971, in that order.
frame.conditions: Confidence depends on the credibility of the official gold-conversion promise.
frame.atmosphere: International trade needs usable balances while official holders seek dependable backing.

frame.process: Explain the conversion rate and the Dollar's reserve-currency role.
frame.how: Build conversion arithmetic and distinguish reserve assets from payments using them.
frame.when: Under the historical gold-linked arrangement, before the 1971 break.
frame.conditions: Conversion applied mainly to foreign central banks; numerical transactions are hypothetical.
frame.atmosphere: French and US authorities settle gold claims and machinery payments through banks.

frame.process: Explain why increasing external Dollar claims strained confidence in gold redemption.
frame.how: Compare the gold needed for claims with available gold, then contrast liquidity with confidence.
frame.when: Pressures accumulated by the 1960s, before the 1971 decision.
frame.conditions: The conflict appears when external claims grow without sufficient growth in gold.
frame.atmosphere: Trade expands while official holders worry about the conversion promise.

frame.process: Read the gold–Dollar–other currencies hierarchy.
frame.how: Trace the three boxes and two arrows from top to bottom.
frame.when: Read as a relationship within the arrangement, not a chronology.
frame.conditions: Arrows indicate monetary links, not physical gold shipments or retail conversion rights.
frame.atmosphere: A three-level diagram connects a familiar Rupee to the international monetary anchor.

frame.process: Connect the 1973 oil shock with the 1974 Saudi–US understanding.
frame.how: Explain restricted supply, higher prices, Saudi financial commitments and US security commitments.
frame.when: 1973 precedes the 1974 understanding.
frame.conditions: Pricing and investment are separate commitments; illustrative allocations are not historical shares.
frame.atmosphere: Oil importers face expensive supplies while Saudi Arabia and the US exchange financial and security commitments.

frame.process: Explain continuing Dollar demand from oil-payment requirements.
frame.how: Follow an enlarged Dollar invoice through a bank into payment demand.
frame.when: After gold convertibility ends, whenever oil invoices require Dollars.
frame.conditions: Dollar pricing is neither oil redemption nor a guarantee of exchange-value stability.
frame.atmosphere: An Indian oil importer obtains foreign currency to pay a seller.

frame.process: Answer why Dollars could still be held without gold backing.
frame.how: Apply the distinction between redemption backing and transaction demand.
frame.when: After teaching the oil-payment channel.

beats.say: Gold link टूटने के बाद भी दुनिया को Dollars क्यों चाहिए रहे?
beats.on_screen: Trade-payment need versus gold-conversion confidence.

beats.say: देशों की currencies कैसे जुड़ी थीं? 1944 के Bretton Woods System में gold से Dollar, उससे बाकी currencies जुड़ी थीं।
beats.on_screen: 1944: gold → Dollar → other currencies.

beats.say: French authority Dollars देकर क्या पाएगी? मान लो उसने US$350 के claims सौंपे और बदले में 10 troy ounces gold लिया।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical official conversion: authority presents US$350 of claims and receives 10 troy ounces.

beats.say: यही fixed gold convertibility है: यानी US$35 देकर 1 troy ounce gold लेना। वादा खासकर foreign central banks के लिए था, आम ग्राहक के लिए नहीं।
beats.on_screen: US$35 ↔ 1 troy ounce; mainly foreign central banks, not a retail entitlement.

beats.say: Machinery bill कैसे भरें? मान लो French importer ने bank को local payment दिया। Authority ने अपने US$700 में से US$350 दिए; bank ने exporter को चुकाए, authority के US$350 बचे।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical, without offsetting inflows: authority supplies US$350 from US$700; bank pays exporter; US$350 remains.

beats.say: Dollar world's reserve currency बना: यानी authorities विदेश के bills भरने लायक assets Dollar में रखती थीं।
beats.on_screen: Reserve currency: official assets usable for international payments.

beats.say: Troy ounce gold तौलने की unit है, करीब 31.1 grams; 10 ऐसे ounces करीब 311 grams हैं।
beats.on_screen: 1 troy ounce ≈ 31.1 g; 10 ≈ 311 g.

beats.say: US$35 historical rate है; French transactions teaching examples हैं। Diagram में बीच की जगह और trade की जरूरत Dollar का central role दिखाते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Historical conversion rate; illustrative transaction amounts. Dollar connects gold and currencies.

beats.say: Gold मिलने का भरोसा confidence देता था; बढ़ते trade को payment balances चाहिए थे। Reserve stock है, payment flow है।
beats.on_screen: Credible conversion → confidence; trade → balance needs. Stock ≠ flow.

beats.say: US$350 को US$35 per troy ounce से बाँटें तो 10 troy ounces मिलते हैं। Import payment में gold नहीं मिलता।
beats.on_screen: Gold received = eligible Dollar claim ÷ US$35 per troy ounce.

beats.say: Claims बढ़ें, gold नहीं, तो? मान लो US buyer ने French machinery के US$350 दिए। French authority ने banks से ये Dollars लिए; पहले US$350 थे, अब US$700 हैं।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: US buyer pays French exporter; French authority acquires proceeds through banks, adding US$350 to existing US$350.

beats.say: US के पास 10 troy ounces ही हैं, लेकिन पूरे claims चुकाने को 20 चाहिए। Authority US$350 बदलकर 10 ounces ले जाए, तो US का gold खत्म होगा, US$350 का दावा फिर भी बचेगा।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: US$700 requires 20 troy ounces. Redeeming US$350 uses the available 10; US$350 remains outstanding.

beats.say: 1960s में US ने Vietnam War और welfare programs पर खूब खर्च किया। बाहर Dollars बढ़े, gold कम पड़ा; जैसे रसीदें ज्यादा, पीछे माल कम। इसलिए France ने gold माँगा।
beats.on_screen: 1960s: heavy US spending; external Dollar claims outgrow available gold backing. Image: more claims than the stock can redeem. France demands gold.

beats.say: Trade बढ़े तो? मान लो French authority अब US$350 नहीं, US$700 रखना चाहती है। उसने export payments के US$350 और लिए। US का gold 10 troy ounces ही रहा; पूरे conversion को 20 चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: authority seeks US$700 and acquires an additional US$350 from export payments. Available gold remains 10 troy ounces; full conversion requires 20.

beats.say: Economist Robert Triffin का built-in contradiction यही है: यानी एक जरूरत पूरी करो, दूसरी कमजोर पड़े। Dollars बढ़ाओ तो payments आसान, gold मिलने का भरोसा कमजोर; रोक दो तो trade के पैसे कम।
beats.on_screen: Triffin dilemma: supplying payment balances versus confidence in gold redemption.

beats.say: France ने कमजोरी बनाई नहीं, सामने लाई: दावों के बदले gold माँगा तो पीछे रखा gold कम पड़ा।
beats.on_screen: Redemption reveals the pre-existing mismatch between claims and gold.

beats.say: Domestic खर्च अपने-आप foreign claim नहीं; international payments बीच की कड़ी हैं। Dollars और gold की तुलना conversion rate से करो।
beats.on_screen: External payments connect spending to foreign balances; compare claims with gold required.

beats.say: Claims बढ़े, gold नहीं बढ़ा, तो conversion का भरोसा घटा।
beats.on_screen: Trade ↑ → claims ↑ → gold pressure ↑ → confidence ↓.

beats.say: 3 boxes में बीच की कड़ी कौन? Diagram gold, Dollar और बाकी currencies का रिश्ता दिखाता है।
beats.on_screen: Show the three-box monetary hierarchy.

beats.say: ऊपर Gold, US$35 per ounce है; ounce यहाँ troy ounce है। Arrow Dollar को gold से जोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Top box: Gold, US$35 per troy ounce → US Dollar.

beats.say: बीच में Dollar ऊपर gold, नीचे currencies जोड़ता है; उसके भरोसे का असर US के बाहर भी पड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Highlight Dollar as the bridge between the two levels.

beats.say: नीचे Pound, Rupee, Yen, Franc जैसे पैसे Dollar से जुड़े हैं। यानी अपना Rupee दिखना, अपने bank से US gold मिलने का हक नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Other currencies → immediate link is Dollar, not a separate gold arrow.

beats.say: Arrows monetary links हैं, gold भेजने का रास्ता या currencies बनने का क्रम नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Links, not shipments or chronology.

beats.say: Gold → Dollar → Pound, Rupee, Yen, Franc का जोड़ याद रखो।
beats.on_screen: Complete labelled three-level diagram.

beats.say: 1960s में बढ़ते claims और gold demands से 1944 का conversion वादा निभाना मुश्किल हुआ।
beats.on_screen: 1944 arrangement → 1960s pressure → policy decision.

beats.say: President Richard Nixon ने official gold conversion बंद किया, यानी Dollar claim देकर gold निकालने वाला रास्ता बंद।
beats.on_screen: Close the official Dollar-to-gold redemption window.

beats.say: Turning point था 15 August 1971: gold–Dollar की ऊपर वाली कड़ी टूटी।
beats.on_screen: 15 August 1971: sever the top arrow.

beats.say: Dollars या सारे institutions खत्म नहीं हुए। सवाल उठा: gold न मिले तो Dollars क्यों रखें? आगे oil payments समझेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Gold conversion ends; continuing Dollar demand becomes the next question.

beats.say: 1944 में ढाँचा बना; 1960s में दबाव बढ़ा; 1971 में conversion बंद हुआ।
Oil कम मिले तो? Mumbai का example लो: पहले 100 barrels आते थे, अब exporters सिर्फ 60 भेजते हैं। मान लो पहले $1 में मिलने वाला barrel अब $4 का है; 10 barrels के पहले $10 देते थे, अब $40 देने पड़ेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical, not 1973 data: exporters deliver 60 rather than 100 barrels; assumed price $4 rather than $1; a 10-barrel order costs $40 rather than $10.

beats.say: बेचने-भेजने पर रोक embargo है। 1973 के OPEC oil embargo में prices 4 गुना हुए; Arab exporters की रोक से supply घटी, fuel चाहिए रहा।
beats.on_screen: 1973 oil embargo: restricted supply, continuing fuel needs, prices ×4.

beats.say: 4 गुना यानी 300% increase, 400% नहीं। Supply घटने से ठीक 4 गुना price होना कोई formula नहीं।
Oil के Dollars कहाँ जाएँ? मान लो Saudi seller $100 पाए, नए Treasury issue में $60 लगाए, $40 रखे; सरकार $60 उधार पाए।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: receipts $100 → cash $40 + Treasury debt asset $60; government borrowing $60.

beats.say: यह receipts का investment है। 1974 में Saudi Arabia ने Dollar oil-pricing और revenues का बड़ा हिस्सा US Treasury securities तथा American financial markets में लगाना माना; 60/40 सिर्फ example है।
beats.on_screen: Separate Dollar pricing from subsequent investment; no historical 60/40 share claimed.

beats.say: बदले में US ने क्या माना? Military protection, weapons और Saudi monarchy को security guarantees, यानी खतरे में मदद का भरोसा।
beats.on_screen: US side: military protection, weapons supply, security guarantees.

beats.say: 1974 में financial और security commitments जुड़े; payment और investment अलग रहे।
beats.on_screen: Financial commitments ↔ security commitments; payment ≠ investment.

beats.say: Treasury securities सरकार के उधार की receipt जैसी हैं। नया issue सरकार को पैसा देता है; पुराना खरीदो तो seller को।
beats.on_screen: New issue → government borrowing; secondary purchase → existing holder.

beats.say: 1973 में oil shock आया; 1974 में Saudi financial और US security commitments जुड़े।
beats.on_screen: 1973 shock → 1974 reciprocal commitments.

beats.say: Order दोगुना हो तो? मान लो Indian importer ने उसी unit price पर दोगुना oil मँगाया। पहले $100 चुकाता था; अब $200 का bill आया, तो उसने bank से $200 जुटाए।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: importer doubles order at unchanged unit price, receives a $200 invoice instead of $100, and obtains $200 through bank.

beats.say: यही oil-payment channel है: US ने समझा, Dollar में oil bills हों तो gold backing बिना भी Dollars चाहिए होंगे।
beats.on_screen: Dollar-priced oil → Dollar payment needs, independent of gold conversion.

beats.say: Dollars export earnings, borrowing, reserves या exchange से मिलें; invoice चुकाने के लिए उनका balance चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Obtain Dollars → settle Dollar invoice.

beats.say: Oil-import news में Dollars bill भरने के लिए चाहिए, gold लेने के लिए नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Oil bills create foreign-exchange needs.

beats.say: Oil pricing backing नहीं: Dollar देकर fixed oil मिलने का promise नहीं। Demand से exchange value कभी न गिरने की guarantee भी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Dollar pricing ≠ oil redemption ≠ guaranteed exchange value.

beats.say: Dollar invoice चुकाना है, इसलिए Dollars चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Oil need → Dollar invoice → Dollar demand.

beats.say: Gold बिना Dollars क्यों रखें? मान लो importer ने नया oil order दिया और $100 का bill पाया। उसने bank से $100 माँगे: exam में backing और payment use अलग रखो।
beats.on_screen: Conceptual exam question: losing gold redemption does not eliminate transaction demand.

beats.say: Gold link टूटने के बाद भी दुनिया को Dollars क्यों चाहिए रहे?
beats.on_screen: Trade-payment need versus gold-conversion confidence.

beats.say: देशों की currencies कैसे जुड़ी थीं? 1944 के Bretton Woods System में gold से Dollar, उससे बाकी currencies जुड़ी थीं।
beats.on_screen: 1944: gold → Dollar → other currencies.

beats.say: French authority Dollars देकर क्या पाएगी? मान लो उसने US$350 के claims सौंपे और बदले में 10 troy ounces gold लिया।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical official conversion: authority presents US$350 of claims and receives 10 troy ounces.

beats.say: यही fixed gold convertibility है: यानी US$35 देकर 1 troy ounce gold लेना। वादा खासकर foreign central banks के लिए था, आम ग्राहक के लिए नहीं।
beats.on_screen: US$35 ↔ 1 troy ounce; mainly foreign central banks, not a retail entitlement.

beats.say: Machinery bill कैसे भरें? मान लो French importer ने bank को local payment दिया। Authority ने अपने US$700 में से US$350 दिए; bank ने exporter को चुकाए, authority के US$350 बचे।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical, without offsetting inflows: authority supplies US$350 from US$700; bank pays exporter; US$350 remains.

beats.say: Dollar world's reserve currency बना: यानी authorities विदेश के bills भरने लायक assets Dollar में रखती थीं।
beats.on_screen: Reserve currency: official assets usable for international payments.

beats.say: Troy ounce gold तौलने की unit है, करीब 31.1 grams; 10 ऐसे ounces करीब 311 grams हैं।
beats.on_screen: 1 troy ounce ≈ 31.1 g; 10 ≈ 311 g.

beats.say: US$35 historical rate है; French transactions teaching examples हैं। Diagram में बीच की जगह और trade की जरूरत Dollar का central role दिखाते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Historical conversion rate; illustrative transaction amounts. Dollar connects gold and currencies.

beats.say: Gold मिलने का भरोसा confidence देता था; बढ़ते trade को payment balances चाहिए थे। Reserve stock है, payment flow है।
beats.on_screen: Credible conversion → confidence; trade → balance needs. Stock ≠ flow.

beats.say: US$350 को US$35 per troy ounce से बाँटें तो 10 troy ounces मिलते हैं। Import payment में gold नहीं मिलता।
beats.on_screen: Gold received = eligible Dollar claim ÷ US$35 per troy ounce.

beats.say: Claims बढ़ें, gold नहीं, तो? मान लो US buyer ने French machinery के US$350 दिए। French authority ने banks से ये Dollars लिए; पहले US$350 थे, अब US$700 हैं।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: US buyer pays French exporter; French authority acquires proceeds through banks, adding US$350 to existing US$350.

beats.say: US के पास 10 troy ounces ही हैं, लेकिन पूरे claims चुकाने को 20 चाहिए। Authority US$350 बदलकर 10 ounces ले जाए, तो US का gold खत्म होगा, US$350 का दावा फिर भी बचेगा।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: US$700 requires 20 troy ounces. Redeeming US$350 uses the available 10; US$350 remains outstanding.

beats.say: 1960s में US ने Vietnam War और welfare programs पर खूब खर्च किया। बाहर Dollars बढ़े, gold कम पड़ा; जैसे रसीदें ज्यादा, पीछे माल कम। इसलिए France ने gold माँगा।
beats.on_screen: 1960s: heavy US spending; external Dollar claims outgrow available gold backing. Image: more claims than the stock can redeem. France demands gold.

beats.say: Trade बढ़े तो? मान लो French authority को अब US$700 चाहिए; पहले US$350 थे। उसने export payments के US$350 और लिए। Gold 10 troy ounces रहा, पूरे conversion को 20 चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: authority seeks US$700 and acquires an additional US$350 from export payments. Available gold remains 10 troy ounces; full conversion requires 20.

beats.say: Economist Robert Triffin का built-in contradiction यही है: एक जरूरत पूरी करो, दूसरी कमजोर पड़े। Dollars बढ़ाओ तो payments आसान, conversion का भरोसा कमजोर; रोक दो तो trade के पैसे कम।
beats.on_screen: Triffin dilemma: supplying payment balances versus confidence in gold redemption.

beats.say: France ने कमजोरी बनाई नहीं, सामने लाई: दावों के बदले gold माँगा तो पीछे रखा gold कम पड़ा।
beats.on_screen: Redemption reveals the pre-existing mismatch between claims and gold.

beats.say: Domestic खर्च अपने-आप foreign claim नहीं; international payments बीच की कड़ी हैं। Dollars और gold की तुलना conversion rate से करो।
beats.on_screen: External payments connect spending to foreign balances; compare claims with gold required.

beats.say: Claims बढ़े, gold नहीं बढ़ा, तो conversion का भरोसा घटा।
beats.on_screen: Trade ↑ → claims ↑ → gold pressure ↑ → confidence ↓.

beats.say: 3 boxes में बीच की कड़ी कौन? Diagram gold, Dollar और बाकी currencies का रिश्ता दिखाता है।
beats.on_screen: Show the three-box monetary hierarchy.

beats.say: ऊपर Gold, US$35 per ounce है; ounce यहाँ troy ounce है। Arrow Dollar को gold से जोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Top box: Gold, US$35 per troy ounce → US Dollar.

beats.say: बीच में Dollar ऊपर gold, नीचे currencies जोड़ता है; उसके भरोसे का असर US के बाहर भी पड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Highlight Dollar as the bridge between the two levels.

beats.say: नीचे Pound, Rupee, Yen, Franc जैसे पैसे Dollar से जुड़े हैं। यानी अपना Rupee दिखना, अपने bank से US gold मिलने का हक नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Other currencies → immediate link is Dollar, not a separate gold arrow.

beats.say: Arrows monetary links हैं, gold भेजने का रास्ता या currencies बनने का क्रम नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Links, not shipments or chronology.

beats.say: Gold → Dollar → Pound, Rupee, Yen, Franc का जोड़ याद रखो।
beats.on_screen: Complete labelled three-level diagram.

beats.say: 1960s में बढ़ते claims और gold demands से 1944 का conversion वादा निभाना मुश्किल हुआ।
beats.on_screen: 1944 arrangement → 1960s pressure → policy decision.

beats.say: President Richard Nixon ने official gold conversion बंद किया, यानी Dollar claim देकर gold निकालने वाला रास्ता बंद।
beats.on_screen: Close the official Dollar-to-gold redemption window.

beats.say: Turning point था 15 August 1971: gold–Dollar की ऊपर वाली कड़ी टूटी।
beats.on_screen: 15 August 1971: sever the top arrow.

beats.say: Dollars या सारे institutions खत्म नहीं हुए। सवाल उठा: gold न मिले तो Dollars क्यों रखें? आगे oil payments समझेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Gold conversion ends; continuing Dollar demand becomes the next question.

beats.say: 1944 में ढाँचा बना; 1960s में दबाव बढ़ा; 1971 में conversion बंद हुआ।
Oil कम मिले तो? Mumbai का example लो: पहले exporters 100 barrels भेजते थे, अब 60 भेजते हैं। मान लो $1 वाला barrel अब $4 में मिले; 10 barrels के पहले $10 देते थे, अब $40 देंगे।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical, not 1973 data: exporters deliver 60 rather than 100 barrels; assumed price $4 rather than $1; a 10-barrel order costs $40 rather than $10.

beats.say: बेचने-भेजने पर रोक embargo है। 1973 के OPEC oil embargo में prices 4 गुना हुए; Arab exporters की रोक से supply घटी, fuel चाहिए रहा।
beats.on_screen: 1973 oil embargo: restricted supply, continuing fuel needs, prices ×4.

beats.say: 4 गुना यानी 300% increase, 400% नहीं। Supply घटने से ठीक 4 गुना price होना कोई formula नहीं।
Oil के Dollars कहाँ जाएँ? मान लो Saudi seller $100 पाए, नए Treasury issue में $60 लगाए, $40 रखे; सरकार $60 उधार पाए।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: receipts $100 → cash $40 + Treasury debt asset $60; government borrowing $60.

beats.say: यह receipts का investment है। 1974 में Saudi Arabia ने Dollar oil-pricing और revenues का बड़ा हिस्सा US Treasury securities तथा American financial markets में लगाना माना; 60/40 सिर्फ example है।
beats.on_screen: Separate Dollar pricing from subsequent investment; no historical 60/40 share claimed.

beats.say: बदले में US ने क्या माना? Military protection, weapons और Saudi monarchy को security guarantees, यानी खतरे में मदद का भरोसा।
beats.on_screen: US side: military protection, weapons supply, security guarantees.

beats.say: 1974 में financial और security commitments जुड़े; payment और investment अलग रहे।
beats.on_screen: Financial commitments ↔ security commitments; payment ≠ investment.

beats.say: Treasury securities सरकार के उधार की receipt जैसी हैं। नया issue सरकार को पैसा देता है; पुराना खरीदो तो seller को।
beats.on_screen: New issue → government borrowing; secondary purchase → existing holder.

beats.say: 1973 में oil shock आया; 1974 में Saudi financial और US security commitments जुड़े।
beats.on_screen: 1973 shock → 1974 reciprocal commitments.

beats.say: Order दोगुना हो तो? मान लो Indian importer ने उसी unit price पर दोगुना oil लिया। पहले $100 देता था; अब $200 चुकाने के लिए bank से $200 जुटाए।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: importer doubles order at unchanged unit price, receives a $200 invoice instead of $100, and obtains $200 through bank.

beats.say: यही oil-payment channel है: US ने समझा, Dollar में oil bills हों तो gold backing बिना भी Dollars चाहिए होंगे।
beats.on_screen: Dollar-priced oil → Dollar payment needs, independent of gold conversion.

beats.say: Dollars export earnings, borrowing, reserves या exchange से मिलें; invoice चुकाने के लिए उनका balance चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Obtain Dollars → settle Dollar invoice.

beats.say: Oil-import news में Dollars bill भरने के लिए चाहिए, gold लेने के लिए नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Oil bills create foreign-exchange needs.

beats.say: Oil pricing backing नहीं: Dollar देकर fixed oil मिलने का promise नहीं। Demand से exchange value कभी न गिरने की guarantee भी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Dollar pricing ≠ oil redemption ≠ guaranteed exchange value.

beats.say: Dollar invoice चुकाना है, इसलिए Dollars चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Oil need → Dollar invoice → Dollar demand.

beats.say: Gold बिना Dollars क्यों रखें? मान लो importer ने नया oil order दिया और $100 का bill पाया। उसने bank से $100 माँगे: exam में backing और payment use अलग रखो।
beats.on_screen: Conceptual exam question: losing gold redemption does not eliminate transaction demand.

beats.say: Dollar world's reserve currency बना: यानी authorities विदेश के bills भरने लायक assets Dollar में रखती थीं।
beats.on_screen: Reserve currency: official assets usable for international payments.

beats.say: Troy ounce gold तौलने की unit है, करीब 31.1 grams; 10 ऐसे ounces करीब 311 grams हैं।
beats.on_screen: 1 troy ounce ≈ 31.1 g; 10 ≈ 311 g.

beats.say: US$35 historical rate है; French transactions teaching examples हैं। Diagram में बीच की जगह और trade की जरूरत Dollar का central role दिखाते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Historical conversion rate; illustrative transaction amounts. Dollar connects gold and currencies.

beats.say: Gold मिलने का भरोसा confidence देता था; बढ़ते trade को payment balances चाहिए थे। Reserve stock है, payment flow है।
beats.on_screen: Credible conversion → confidence; trade → balance needs. Stock ≠ flow.

beats.say: US$350 को US$35 per troy ounce से बाँटें तो 10 troy ounces मिलते हैं। Import payment में gold नहीं मिलता।
beats.on_screen: Gold received = eligible Dollar claim ÷ US$35 per troy ounce.

beats.say: Claims बढ़ें, gold नहीं, तो? मान लो US buyer ने French machinery के US$350 दिए। French authority ने banks से ये Dollars लिए; पहले US$350 थे, अब US$700 हैं।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: US buyer pays French exporter; French authority acquires proceeds through banks, adding US$350 to existing US$350.

beats.say: US के पास 10 troy ounces ही हैं, लेकिन पूरे claims चुकाने को 20 चाहिए। Authority US$350 बदलकर 10 ounces ले जाए, तो US का gold खत्म होगा, US$350 का दावा फिर भी बचेगा।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: US$700 requires 20 troy ounces. Redeeming US$350 uses the available 10; US$350 remains outstanding.

beats.say: 1960s में US ने Vietnam War और welfare programs पर खूब खर्च किया। बाहर Dollars बढ़े, gold कम पड़ा; जैसे रसीदें ज्यादा, पीछे माल कम। इसलिए France ने gold माँगा।
beats.on_screen: 1960s: heavy US spending; external Dollar claims outgrow available gold backing. Image: more claims than the stock can redeem. France demands gold.

beats.say: Trade बढ़े तो? मान लो French authority को अब US$700 चाहिए; पहले US$350 थे। उसने export payments के US$350 और लिए। Gold 10 troy ounces रहा, पूरे conversion को 20 चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: authority seeks US$700 and acquires an additional US$350 from export payments. Available gold remains 10 troy ounces; full conversion requires 20.

beats.say: Robert Triffin ने यही built-in contradiction बताया: यानी trade के लिए रसीदें बढ़ाओ, तो पीछे कम gold देखकर भरोसा घटे; रोकें तो payments अटकें।
beats.on_screen: Triffin: more payment claims against unchanged gold weaken redemption confidence; restricting claims constrains payments.

beats.say: France ने कमजोरी बनाई नहीं, सामने लाई: दावों के बदले gold माँगा तो पीछे रखा gold कम पड़ा।
beats.on_screen: Redemption reveals the pre-existing mismatch between claims and gold.

beats.say: Domestic खर्च अपने-आप foreign claim नहीं; international payments बीच की कड़ी हैं। Dollars और gold की तुलना conversion rate से करो।
beats.on_screen: External payments connect spending to foreign balances; compare claims with gold required.

beats.say: Claims बढ़े, gold नहीं बढ़ा, तो conversion का भरोसा घटा।
beats.on_screen: Trade ↑ → claims ↑ → gold pressure ↑ → confidence ↓.

beats.say: 3 boxes में बीच की कड़ी कौन? Diagram gold, Dollar और बाकी currencies का रिश्ता दिखाता है।
beats.on_screen: Show the three-box monetary hierarchy.

beats.say: ऊपर Gold, US$35 per ounce है; ounce यहाँ troy ounce है। Arrow Dollar को gold से जोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Top box: Gold, US$35 per troy ounce → US Dollar.

beats.say: बीच में Dollar ऊपर gold, नीचे currencies जोड़ता है; उसके भरोसे का असर US के बाहर भी पड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Highlight Dollar as the bridge between the two levels.

beats.say: नीचे Pound, Rupee, Yen, Franc जैसे पैसे Dollar से जुड़े हैं। यानी अपना Rupee दिखना, अपने bank से US gold मिलने का हक नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Other currencies → immediate link is Dollar, not a separate gold arrow.

beats.say: Arrows monetary links हैं, gold भेजने का रास्ता या currencies बनने का क्रम नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Links, not shipments or chronology.

beats.say: Gold → Dollar → Pound, Rupee, Yen, Franc का जोड़ याद रखो।
beats.on_screen: Complete labelled three-level diagram.

beats.say: 1960s में बढ़ते claims और gold demands से 1944 का conversion वादा निभाना मुश्किल हुआ।
beats.on_screen: 1944 arrangement → 1960s pressure → policy decision.

beats.say: President Richard Nixon ने official gold conversion बंद किया, यानी Dollar claim देकर gold निकालने वाला रास्ता बंद।
beats.on_screen: Close the official Dollar-to-gold redemption window.

beats.say: Turning point था 15 August 1971: gold–Dollar की ऊपर वाली कड़ी टूटी।
beats.on_screen: 15 August 1971: sever the top arrow.

beats.say: Conversion बंद हुआ, Dollars या सारे institutions नहीं। अब सवाल था: gold बिना Dollars क्यों रखें? जवाब oil payments से जुड़ेगा।
beats.on_screen: Gold conversion ends; continuing Dollar demand becomes the next question.

beats.say: 1944 में ढाँचा बना; 1960s में दबाव बढ़ा; 1971 में conversion बंद हुआ।
Oil कम मिले तो? Mumbai का example लो: पहले exporters 100 barrels भेजते थे, अब 60 भेजते हैं। मान लो $1 वाला barrel अब $4 में मिले; 10 barrels के पहले $10 देते थे, अब $40 देंगे।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical, not 1973 data: exporters deliver 60 rather than 100 barrels; assumed price $4 rather than $1; a 10-barrel order costs $40 rather than $10.

beats.say: बेचने-भेजने पर रोक embargo है। 1973 के OPEC oil embargo में prices 4 गुना हुए; Arab exporters की रोक से supply घटी, fuel चाहिए रहा।
beats.on_screen: 1973 oil embargo: restricted supply, continuing fuel needs, prices ×4.

beats.say: 4 गुना यानी 300% increase, 400% नहीं। Supply घटने से ठीक 4 गुना price होना कोई formula नहीं।
Oil के Dollars कहाँ जाएँ? मान लो Saudi seller $100 पाए, नए Treasury issue में $60 लगाए, $40 रखे; सरकार $60 उधार पाए।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: receipts $100 → cash $40 + Treasury debt asset $60; government borrowing $60.

beats.say: यह receipts का investment है। 1974 में Saudi Arabia ने Dollar oil-pricing और revenues का बड़ा हिस्सा US Treasury securities तथा American financial markets में लगाना माना; 60/40 सिर्फ example है।
beats.on_screen: Separate Dollar pricing from subsequent investment; no historical 60/40 share claimed.

beats.say: बदले में US ने क्या माना? Military protection, weapons और Saudi monarchy को security guarantees, यानी खतरे में मदद का भरोसा।
beats.on_screen: US side: military protection, weapons supply, security guarantees.

beats.say: 1974 में पैसे और सुरक्षा के वादे जुड़े; bill चुकाना, receipts invest करना अलग काम रहे।
beats.on_screen: 1974: financial commitments ↔ security commitments; payment ≠ investment.

beats.say: Treasury securities सरकार के उधार की receipt जैसी हैं। नया issue सरकार को पैसा देता है; पुराना खरीदो तो seller को।
beats.on_screen: New issue → government borrowing; secondary purchase → existing holder.

beats.say: 1973 में oil shock आया; 1974 में Saudi financial और US security commitments जुड़े।
beats.on_screen: 1973 shock → 1974 reciprocal commitments.

beats.say: Order दोगुना हो तो? मान लो Indian importer ने उसी unit price पर दोगुना oil लिया। पहले $100 देता था; अब $200 चुकाने के लिए bank से $200 जुटाए।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical: importer doubles order at unchanged unit price, receives a $200 invoice instead of $100, and obtains $200 through bank.

beats.say: यही oil-payment channel है: US ने समझा, Dollar में oil bills हों तो gold backing बिना भी Dollars चाहिए होंगे।
beats.on_screen: Dollar-priced oil → Dollar payment needs, independent of gold conversion.

beats.say: Dollars export earnings, borrowing, reserves या exchange से मिलें; invoice चुकाने के लिए उनका balance चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Obtain Dollars → settle Dollar invoice.

beats.say: Oil-import news में Dollars bill भरने के लिए चाहिए, gold लेने के लिए नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Oil bills create foreign-exchange needs.

beats.say: Oil pricing backing नहीं: Dollar देकर fixed oil मिलने का promise नहीं। Demand से exchange value कभी न गिरने की guarantee भी नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Dollar pricing ≠ oil redemption ≠ guaranteed exchange value.

beats.say: Dollar invoice चुकाना है, इसलिए Dollars चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Oil need → Dollar invoice → Dollar demand.

beats.say: Gold बिना Dollars क्यों रखें? मान लो importer ने नया oil order दिया और $100 का bill पाया। उसने bank से $100 माँगे: exam में backing और payment use अलग रखो।
beats.on_screen: Conceptual exam question: losing gold redemption does not eliminate transaction demand.

notes.about: This unit explains the gold–Dollar arrangement, its internal tension and the 1971 conversion decision, then connects oil payments and Saudi investment commitments to continuing Dollar demand.
key_questions: Who could exchange Dollars for gold, and at what rate?
Why did supplying Dollars for trade weaken confidence in gold conversion?
What precisely ended on 15 August 1971?
How did oil pricing and investment create distinct channels supporting Dollar use?
